doc.title: Horn Shirley — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Fear of thunderstorms and a blackout during filming
summary: She turns off the phone in storms and recalls a storm that cut the power during a filmed interview.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Here, let me tell you a little something now. See, when I was a little girl, when it was lightning and thunder, you know . . .
We have to stop, that‘s what you‘re . . .
I knew exactly when you started in . . .
Yeah, don‘t talk on the phone.
Right. No, my great-grandmother, you would get your hands popped if you even thought about it.
We would sit in the dark on this small little house on 12th Street, and I‘d be so mad. I‘d be like, ―Why can‘t we even watch TV?‖ But you don‘t do it. You just sit there.
You know, go to bed, whatever you want to do.
When I‘m alone, I get in the bed.
Yes, no, I saw the lightning.

Yeah. And, you know, we had the worst storm when we were recording here, and everything was plugged in. TV cameras were in there, and this guy was trying to do an interview with me, and I kept . . . I said, ―Whoa. Stop.‖ But God took care of that. He just turned everything off.
That‘s right. We had a complete blowout, the biggest night here. So I had candles and we just worked the bar. [laughs] Everybody had a good time. Richard Seidel was here.
I can‘t tell you exactly what I said, but it was, ―You can‘t mess with that. Ain‘t a damn thing you . . .‖ Everything went off, the streetlights, everything.
